assertion: An event exists, described as "Last summer's heatwave".

assertion: An event exists, described as "Europe's warming trend".
judge_quote: Europe has warmed at roughly twice the global average since the 1980s
evidence_cited: Europe has warmed at roughly twice the global average since the 1980s, according to the European Commission’s climate change service, Copernicus. || And because Europe is warming roughly twice as fast as the rest of the planet, that gap with the global average is projected to keep widening – meaning whatever the world experiences on average in the coming decades, Europe will likely see first, and worse.

assertion: An event exists, described as "Alpine glacier loss".
judge_quote: record Alpine glacier loss

assertion: An event exists, described as "Heat-related deaths".
judge_quote: The Lancet Countdown Europe calculates that there were 62,000 heat-related deaths across the region in 2024 alone
evidence_cited: The Lancet Countdown Europe calculates that there were 62,000 heat-related deaths across the region in 2024 alone, with projections showing a steep further rise by 2050 if we don’t make changes. || Deaths have already risen by an average of 52 per million people annually since the 1990s, he told Al Jazeera – a trend he says shows little sign of reversing on its own.

assertion: An event exists, described as "Infrastructure collapse".
judge_quote: the collapse of infrastructure across the continent
evidence_cited: Transport buckled on Sunday as temperatures hit 40C (104F) across Germany, the Czech Republic and Poland.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Heatwaves more likely now".
judge_quote: intense heat on this level is now tens to hundreds of times more likely than it was in 2003
evidence_cited: A study by World Weather Attribution (WWA) has found that intense heat on this level is now tens to hundreds of times more likely than it was in 2003, and was unheard of 50 years ago.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Heat mortality to persist".
judge_quote: Heat-related mortality is likely to remain a feature of Europe’s warming climate
evidence_cited: “Heat-related mortality is likely to remain a feature of Europe’s warming climate,” warns Dr Hans Kluge, the World Health Organization (WHO)’s regional director for Europe.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "New normal for summers".
judge_quote: Scenes like this may well be the new normal.
evidence_cited: Yes, it certainly looks that way. According to WWA, heatwaves were generally about 3.5C cooler in June 1976, and 2C cooler even in 2003.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Global warming as cause".
judge_quote: Ultimately, this is down to global warming
evidence_cited: “Think of it like a race where the starting line has been moved much closer to the finish,” Dr Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading told Al Jazeera. Ultimately, this is down to global warming, he says.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Extremes every couple decades".

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Past emissions cause warming".
judge_quote: the warming behind new, extreme weather patterns comes from emissions released decades ago
evidence_cited: Professor Hannah Cloke of the University of Reading told Al Jazeera that’s because the warming behind new, extreme weather patterns comes from emissions released decades ago, and the climate system takes time to respond – so we’re feeling the effects now of pollution from the past.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Some damage permanent".
judge_quote: Some of the damage is permanent.
evidence_cited: Partly. Some of the damage is permanent. Some of it isn’t – yet. || Because the effects of pollution from decades ago are cumulative, “some of what we are experiencing this summer is already locked in”, Cloke says.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Emissions reduction changes odds".
judge_quote: Every tonne of emissions avoided changes the odds of what comes next
evidence_cited: “Every tonne of emissions avoided changes the odds of what comes next,” Cloke says.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Housing stock unsuitable".

evidence_cited: “Most of the housing stock across this region was designed for a colder climate – to retain heat, not shed it,” he said, warning that without large-scale retrofitting, deaths could keep climbing past 2050 regardless of how good warning systems become.

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Plan for heat like flu".

assertion: A claim exists, described as "Priorities: warnings and water".
